english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{16}=1$ and let $P_1=\left(4,\dfrac{12}{5}\right)$. For each $n\ge1$, the normal to $E$ at $P_n$ meets the $x$-axis at $G_n$, and $P_{n+1}$ is the point of $E$ in the first quadrant whose abscissa is equal to the abscissa of $G_n$. Let $x_n$ denote the abscissa of $P_n$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}x_n$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{25}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{16}=1$ है तथा $P_1=\left(4,\dfrac{12}{5}\right)$ है। प्रत्येक $n\ge1$ के लिए, $P_n$ पर $E$ का अभिलम्ब $x$-अक्ष को $G_n$ पर मिलता है, तथा $P_{n+1}$ प्रथम चतुर्थांश में $E$ का वह बिन्दु है जिसका भुज $G_n$ के भुज के बराबर है। माना $x_n$ बिन्दु $P_n$ का भुज है। तब $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}x_n$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $0<x_{G_n}<5$, so $P_{n+1}$ exists and $x_{n+1}=\dfrac{9}{25}x_n$: a GP with $x_1=4$, ratio $\dfrac{9}{25}$
solution_full: $P_1$ is on $E$: $\dfrac{16}{25}+\dfrac{144/25}{16}=\dfrac{16}{25}+\dfrac{9}{25}=1$. Write a first-quadrant point as $P_n(5\cos\theta_n,4\sin\theta_n)$, $0<\theta_n<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
The normal at the point with eccentric angle $\theta$ is $\dfrac{ax}{\cos\theta}-\dfrac{by}{\sin\theta}=a^{2}-b^{2}$, here $\dfrac{5x}{\cos\theta_n}-\dfrac{4y}{\sin\theta_n}=9$.
Since $0<\dfrac{9}{25}x_n<5$, there is exactly one point of $E$ in the first quadrant with this abscissa, so $P_{n+1}$ is well defined and $x_{n+1}=\dfrac{9}{25}x_n$.
Thus $x_n=4\left(\dfrac{9}{25}\right)^{n-1}$, a geometric progression with ratio less than $1$, and $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}x_n=\dfrac{4}{1-\frac{9}{25}}=\dfrac{100}{16}=\dfrac{25}{4}=6.25$.
originality_note: New: an iteration in which each normal's foot on the major axis becomes the abscissa of the next point, giving a GP with ratio e^2 (way 1, iteration). Closest known: the normal at P meets the major axis at G with CG = e^2 CN. Different because: the standard relation is only one step; the question builds a chain of points and asks for the sum, which needs the relation to be recognised as a contraction.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that P1 lies on E, that every G_n lies strictly between 0 and 5 so P_(n+1) exists and is unique in the first quadrant, and that the sum is exact. Changed: No change.
key_step: The normal's x-intercept is e^2 times the abscissa of the point, so x_(n+1) = (9/25) x_n.
justification: Two ideas linked: the parametric normal and its intercept, then recognising the iteration as a geometric progression; numerical format. Closest in demand to 2023-P1-Q2 (L3), an ellipse question chaining tangent/normal facts.

concept_use.Parametric coordinates for Ellipse: Each P_n is written as (5 cos theta_n, 4 sin theta_n), which makes the normal's x-intercept (9/5) cos theta_n = (9/25) x_n.
concept_use.Tangent and normal for Ellipse: The normal ax/cos theta - by/sin theta = a^2 - b^2 at P_n meets the x-axis at G_n, which defines the next point and the ratio 9/25.
